title: Wi-Fi 7 Explained: Why Multiple Links Matter
headline:
One connection.
More than one lane.
meaning: Multi-Link Operation can use multiple wireless links.
example: A compatible device can avoid a congested link.
comparison: Wi-Fi capacity is different from internet-plan speed.
caution: Both the router and device need compatible support.
question: Is your bottleneck Wi-Fi or internet?
lines: Your wireless connection can feel busy even when your internet plan looks fast. Wi-Fi seven adds another idea.
Multi-Link Operation allows compatible devices to use multiple wireless links instead of relying on just one.
Think of traffic moving through more than one lane, with the exact behavior depending on the hardware.
This can improve reliability and responsiveness. It does not automatically make your internet subscription faster.
Your router, device, surroundings, and local rules all affect which features you can actually use.
